raw_response:
I'm fifty-nine this year, and I've been working this land since I was nineteen. Never spent a day in school, but I know my fourteen mu better than anyone. It's just me now, so I have to be careful — my back isn't what it used to be, and I can't afford to waste a single yuan. I grow a bit of everything because if one crop fails, maybe the other will save me. That's how I've survived forty years.

My wheat and garlic are already in the ground from last fall. The wheat looks all right, not great. I'll give it one more feeding when it greens up — about half a bag of urea per mu, that's what I always do. I'll water it twice more from my well before harvest, but pumping costs electricity, so I watch it. The garlic needs to come out by late May; I'll hire two young people from the village to help dig because my knees can't handle bending all day anymore.

Now for the spring planting. I'm putting cotton on four mu — it's reliable money, and I know how it grows here. I buy the hybrid seed from Old Wang's shop; my own saved seed got weak. I'll spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, then hoe it in. Cotton needs spraying when the bollworm comes, usually three or four times. I'll irrigate twice in summer, when the pods are setting.

Chili is on four mu — that's my main crop, what I know best. I started the seedlings in a small bed behind the house in March. I'll transplant in mid-May, after the garlic is out. I put down some chicken manure and a bit of compound fertilizer at planting, then topdress once when the flowers come. Chili needs water more often, maybe four or five times, especially when it's fruiting. Picking goes on for months; I'll need to hire women from the village for that, or I'll never finish.

Watermelon is just one mu, by the road where my nephew can help me sell. I use plastic mulch to keep the soil warm — bought the film last month, cost me. Lots of manure as base, then some fertilizer. Watermelon is tricky: too dry and they don't grow, too wet and they split. I'll water carefully, maybe three times total.

I save seed when I can — wheat and garlic I use my own. Cotton and watermelon I buy. Fertilizer prices went up again, so I'm using a bit less than I'd like, but I can't risk the yield dropping too much. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps, so I'd rather put down a little extra than too little. I expect wheat around 400 kg per mu, cotton about 300 kg of seed cotton, chili maybe 600 kg fresh, watermelon a few thousand kg, and garlic around 1000 kg. It won't make me rich, but it'll keep me fed.
